questions.question_text:
$F(x) = x^{3} - 4x^{2}$ is a primitive of $f$.
Evaluate $\int_{2}^{5} f(x)\,dx$.

options.why: Subtracted $8$ instead of $-8$, losing the double negative in $25 - (-8)$.
Computed $F(2) - F(5)$, reversing the order of the limits.

questions.question_text: Which function is a primitive of $f(x) = 8x^{3} + 1$?

options.why: Differentiated $f$ instead of finding a function whose derivative is $f$.
Left the constant term $1$ unchanged instead of integrating it to $x$.
Divided by the old index $3$ instead of the new index $4$.

It is positive, because an area can never be negative.
options.why: Confuses geometric area with signed area; a definite integral is negative where the curve lies below the axis.

options.text: It is zero, because the curve meets the $x$-axis at the right-hand end of the interval.
options.why: A crossing at one endpoint does not cancel anything; the whole region still lies below the axis.

options.text: It is positive, because the upper limit is greater than the lower limit.
options.why: The limits are in the correct order, but the sign of a definite integral is set by where the region lies, not by the limits.

questions.solution_text:
Across the shaded interval the curve lies below the $x$-axis, so $f(x)$ is negative there.
The signed area is therefore negative.

questions.question_text:
A machine produces bolts at a rate of $r(t)$ bolts per hour, and $R$ is a primitive of $r$.
Given $R(1) = 140$ and $R(6) = 890$, how many bolts are produced between $t = 1$ and $t = 6$ hours?

options.why: Added the two values of the primitive instead of subtracting them.
Computed $R(1) - R(6)$, reversing the order in $F(b) - F(a)$.
Divided the change by the $5$-hour interval, which gives an average rate rather than a total.

questions.question_text: Find the value of $k > 0$ for which $\int_{0}^{k}(4x + 3)\,dx = 27$.

options.why: Substituted $k$ into the integrand and solved $4k + 3 = 27$ instead of using the primitive.
The other root of $2k^{2} + 3k - 27 = 0$, which must be rejected because $k > 0$.
Divided $27$ by the coefficient $2$ of $k^{2}$ instead of solving the quadratic.
Wrote the limits the wrong way round; the left-hand end of the region is the lower limit.
Used $dy$ although the strips making up the region are measured along the $x$-axis.
Placed a primitive of the function inside the integral sign instead of the function itself.

questions.solution_text:
The shaded region runs from $x = 1$ to $x = 2$, between $y = 5 - 2x$ and the $x$-axis.
Signed area $= \int_{1}^{2}(5 - 2x)\,dx$
